excitation_report: Full child-vs-parent ODE-system comparison on target state I over t in [0, 0.01] s. Peak per-step effect of the new dielectric-memory branch (added terms (Q - Q_m)/C_rel plus the radiation-reaction correction and the extra state Q_m with RHS (Q-Q_m)/tau_rel) is 0.283 A/s at t ~ 1.21 ms, which is 5.66*sigma at sigma = 0.05 A/s (k=5). The dominant capacitive term Q/C over L*f_air is on the order of 10^3 A/s, so the injected noise is ~0.005% of the dominant signal — clean but not unphysically clean for a synthetic circuit dataset. Other pre-existing terms (series_resistance*I, cubic dielectric nonlinearity, saturable-core relaxation) remain visible far above sigma; auto_balance was skipped as it is not supported for ode_system.

rationale: Typed ode_system for a lossy nonlinear LC loop with saturable-core and dielectric-memory extensions; state contract inherited verbatim from the upstream ODE validation. Chose t in [0, 0.01] s (as stated in the phenomenon) with 500 samples to resolve the ~1.4 ms natural period (~35 points/period). Parameter values keep peak current below inductor_saturation_current so the log-saturation is exercised but not violent, keep core_magnetic_relaxation_time and dielectric_relaxation_time comparable to the LC period so both memory branches are dynamically active, and place dielectric_relaxation_capacitance at the low end of the suggested range (1e-5 F) so the new memory term reaches 5.66*sigma at sigma = 0.05 A/s. The dielectric-memory branch has an intrinsically small effect on I(t) because its initial state is at equilibrium with Q, so its influence is bounded no matter how the coefficients are pushed within physical ranges; the low sigma (~0.005% of the dominant signal) is the cost of making the added term unambiguously visible for symbolic regression while keeping every parameter physically meaningful.
